recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. If the work group wants processor-specific warning behavior for ordering-only MeasureReports beyond the current data model and narrative, handle that as a new clarification rather than reopening the already-applied FHIR-38832 source changes.
issue_request: FHIR-38832 was a Published/Persuasive R5 CQI change request to add linkId elements to Measure and MeasureReport group and population elements so MeasureReport content can link explicitly to the corresponding Measure content without relying on non-unique code values or internal Element.id values; its resolution also called for backwards-compatible code, id, and ordering fallback guidance.
initial_application: Jira comment evidence points to commit f9f70c4bbb4606c854d3ed18e86355b9dd2bc70f, which added linkId elements to source/measure/structuredefinition-Measure.xml and source/measurereport/structuredefinition-MeasureReport.xml. The current source retains the requested Measure.group.linkId, Measure.group.population.linkId, MeasureReport.group.linkId, and MeasureReport.group.population.linkId definitions, plus parallel linkIds for stratifier-related and supplementalData elements.
additional_context: Measure and MeasureReport are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Later Applied issue FHIR-49670 clarified the same Measure-to-MeasureReport correspondence area in R6 by strengthening MeasureReport group/population/stratifier and code/description guidance while preserving backwards-compatible id support. The clinical reasoning quality-reporting narrative also explains that group, population, and stratifier linkIds correlate MeasureReport elements back to Measure elements. Community searches found no conflicting FHIR-38832 discussion, and a later Zulip implementation thread described R5 linkId as the explicit replacement for R4 id-based correlation.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative resource definitions and current narrative already convey the concrete linkId mechanism requested by FHIR-38832, preserve backwards-compatible id handling, and include later code/correspondence clarification from FHIR-49670. Adding another fallback-priority paragraph would duplicate existing element-level guidance without correcting a current semantic defect.
